claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you enquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have a son Alex who is 17 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 17 (over 16), I need to ask:

**Is Alex still in approved education or training?** (For example, is he attending college, sixth form, doing A-levels, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He left school and now he's working full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify a bit more about Alex's work situation:

**How many hours per week is Alex working in his full-time job?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's working full-time - that's 24 hours a week or more. I think it's around 35-40 hours actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarize the situation:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He lives at home with you
- He is not in approved education or training
- He is working full-time (35-40 hours per week, which is 24 hours or more)

Based on the rules, when a child who is 16 or over starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training, Child Benefit stops.

Before I provide my final assessment, I need to confirm:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to make a determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.text:
## Assessment Result

Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**

According to Child Benefit rules, you stop getting Child Benefit if your child who is 16 or over starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

In your case:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He is working full-time (35-40 hours per week, which is well over the 24-hour threshold)
- He is not in any approved education or training

Since Alex meets all these criteria, Child Benefit would have stopped when he started working full-time and left education.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he returns to approved education or training and reduces his work hours), you may be able to claim Child Benefit again at that time.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
